title: Validation study for the detection of premalignant/malignant changes in the oesophagus and stomach in risk groups
summary:
The RISC-GAP project aims to develop a way to spot stomach and oesophageal cancer early on. This will be based on the individual risk of people. A two-stage procedure will be used to recognise people with a high risk of early cancer stages or precursors as accurately as possible. Only these people will then be invited for a screening examination (gastroscopy). To work out the risk, we look at things like age and lifestyle, and we also check for new biological signs (called biomarkers). We use information from large studies to create the first risk score. At the heart of the project is a special study where people with a high first risk score get a gastroscopy. These exams are done at specialised medical practices and at Augsburg University Hospital.
500 people between the ages of 50 and 75 will take part in the study. Their samples will be analysed for known and new biomarkers. These biomarkers will then be used to create a second risk score. The aim is to find out how accurately the two scores together can recognise a high-risk group. If this works well, the procedure could be trialled and implemented in a further project.
conditions: Precancerous conditions and carcinomas of the upper gastrointestinal tract (in particular, but not exclusively: intestinal metaplasia, atrophic gastritis, Helicobacter pylori infection, Barrett epithelium, dysplasia, carcinomas)

interventions.name:
1. High risk score 1 (RS1) leads to inclusion in the main study: epidemiological data collection, sampling of biomarkers and esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD)

2. Additional study: Collection of the risk score 1 (RS1) in subjects who have undergone esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) for other reasons

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- People from the general population: participants in organised colorectal cancer screening, patients in general practices, patients in gastroenterological practices who would not undergo an EGD for medical reasons.
- Signed informed consent form
- Presence of a high RS1
Exclusion criteria:
- Subjects unable to give consent
- Presence of a non-high RS1
- Age <50 or >75 years
- EGD within the past 3 years
- Diseases that warrant an endoscopic examination or follow-up of the upper gastrointestinal tract
- Known, active or past tumour diseases of the upper GIT
- Presence of polyposis or Lynch syndrome
- Acute GI haemorrhage (varicose or non-varicose) in the upper GIT
